labels.holds: Cheaper than both in every week
labels.caption: Sensitivity of Sublet on weeks 301--304: its median saving over the all-fallback cost (overflow accounting, the trace lender) per assumption, one assumption at a time, each setting's saving over its own all-fallback cost. A bar runs from the lowest to the highest median over the row's settings (markers) and the default (grey line, 45.8\%), labeled with the settings at its ends; rows sorted by span; one $x$ scale in all panels. Filled: Sublet's cost is below that of both Greedy, back-off and RetroRenting-style in every week (50 of 59 settings); open: not in every week. $\Gamma$ is re-solved to keep the market tightness at its default 0.5 (in its own row, at the row's values) in every row of (b) and in the offered layers $V_\ell$, lease quantile, layer GPUs and buffer quantile rows of (c). L-rf refuses purchases on unavailable layers and L-vr turns buffer violations into reclaims without notice (off: the trace lender; on: the variant); these two rows and the buffer quantile 0.999 reuse the confirmation's runs. Not run: the warm-peer and SSD load-rate scaling, the client unit $1/u$ and the pool width $\zeta$ (no sweep in the register); the tier map (its sweep is the default); a per-tier tokens-per-conversation factor and a clock alignment at local midnight (no source); a non-causal smoothing window and a load scenario per region pair (not built); $V_\ell$ as the whole block below the lease quantile (beyond the evaluation's memory budget); $V_\ell$ as a share of the mean lendable capacity (not defined); a uniform $\kappa$ multiplier (identical to the default).

layout.rule: one x scale in all panels, each its own window; end labels 4.5 pt outside their bars and at least 4 pt inside the axes, markers 4 pt; the data keep at least 0.35 of the axes' total width; gutter 0.14 in; each panel's title within its axes' right end; the legend in a panel with at least 2 free rows where it fits, else in a row above the panels
